messages:
Asha (PM): Heads-up — competitor Y just announced a 'low-latency' tier and a pricing tweak for embeddings. Got a few customer emails already. We should calibrate roadmap impact.
Ben (Eng): Which parts of our roadmap are exposed here? My first thought: Redwood Optimize suggestions and some caching/batching optimizations.
Lee (ML): Signal details: they're pushing a new kernel path that drops tail latency for short sequences ~50%. We still win on throughput for long runs but short prompt latency is their message.
Tara (Sales): Two enterprise trials asked if we can match that 'faster responses' promise. One said they're considering switching if we can't show a plan.
Sam (Design): From the UI side, customers conflate speed with perceived correctness. If we tune purely for latency we need to keep explicit quality cues so users don't assume outputs got worse.
Asha (PM): Propose options: A) Quick parity spike — micro-optimizations (int8 kernel tweak, tiny-batch routing) — ~2 sprints. B) Differentiator path — invest in predictive routing + SLA guarantees — longer, more defensible. Need to pick given sales pressure.
Ben (Eng): Quick estimate: parity spike = ~2 engineers * 2 sprints + infra changes (kernel rollout, flags). Risk: introduces hacky paths. Diff path = multi-sprint work across routing, cache lifecycle, rollout infra.
Lee (ML): For either path we must gate on quality. Suggested guardrails: no >1% regression in token-level perplexity / evaluated prompts. I'll add a focused eval suite.
Tara (Sales): If we offer a limited promise for Dedicated customers (canary/early access) that might buy time. They asked for sub-100ms for short prompts specifically.
Asha (PM): Draft launch criteria for parity spike: 1) median latency <120ms for 16-token queries on target GPU; 2) cost uplift <=10%/token; 3) automated eval pass rate >=99% for regression tests; 4) rollback plan + feature flag. Thoughts?
Ben (Eng): Sounds reasonable. Canary plan: route 5% traffic under `fast_path_v1`, monitor median/tail latency, errors, token cost. We'll add the feature flag and canary hooks.
Sam (Design): I'll draft Console copy: 'Fast response (experimental) — enable per-route'. Need a telemetry toggle and clear experimental badge.
Lee (ML): I'll hook up the perf harness and run baseline vs parity changes. ETA for initial numbers: end of sprint (2 weeks).
Tara (Sales): If we go parity spike, need a one-pager + early access offer for customers on Dedicated. I'll draft and share with legal.
Asha (PM): Decision for now: timebox the parity spike for 2 sprints. If perf or cost metrics fail the gate, we abort and pivot to the predictive-routing differentiator. Action items: Ben — RFC by EOD; Lee — perf harness + eval tests by Wed; Sam — UX copy by Thurs; Tara — customer comms draft by Fri. @OpsBot create board card.
OpsBot: Created ticket PROD-4721 'fast_path_v1 parity spike' and assigned to @Ben (Eng).
Ben (Eng): I’ll take RFC and initial rollout PR. Adding `fast_path_v1` feature flag to the repo and will open draft PR later today.
Asha (PM): Thanks everyone. We’ll review gate metrics in the sprint demo and sync Thurs in roadmap meeting with leadership.
